key_insight: Representing a scene as dynamic 3D Gaussians lets a model convert a single image into camera-controllable video—predicting plausible scene dynamics while rendering novel camera paths with strong 3D and temporal consistency.
problem_solved: Overcomes the lack of user-controllable camera trajectories and limited 3D consistency in single-image-conditioned video generation.
method: Construct a dynamic 3D Gaussian scene representation (spatially localized Gaussian 'splats') inferred from a single input image.
Learn temporal dynamics on the Gaussian representation so the scene can be forecasted over time and rendered from arbitrary camera trajectories.
Train with photometric and temporal-consistency objectives and render efficiently to produce coherent, camera-controlled video sequences.
impact: Enables practitioners to generate realistic, temporally coherent videos from one image with explicit camera control—useful for content creation, AR/VR, and simulation in robotics. It bridges neural rendering and controllable video forecasting for more practical, editable video synthesis.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: single image → infer 3D Gaussians → temporal dynamics module → render frames along a user-defined camera path.
Side-by-side comparison: uncontrolled vs. camera-controlled generated videos highlighting improved 3D consistency.
Camera-path overlay on rendered frames showing viewpoint changes over time.
Bar chart or table of quantitative metrics (temporal coherence, 3D consistency) and a small ablation visualization showing the effect of the dynamic Gaussian component.
paper_title: Pixel-to-4D: Camera-Controlled Image-to-Video Generation with Dynamic 3D Gaussians
paper_authors: Melonie de Almeida, Daniela Ivanova, Tong Shi, John H. Williamson, Paul Henderson
